fullPassage:
Part 1 FOMO (Fear of Missing Out)
"Selena. SELENA!"
"Yes," I look up from my phone to discover my mom yelling at me. She seems to be searching for an answer to something. "What?" I asked.
She asked, "Did you not hear what I just said?"
No, I didn't. I didn't hear anything she said. I usually don't hear a single word said to me by anyone. And why is that? It's because my eyes are fixed on my phone. My mom always asks me, "What is so interesting on your phone?" I never know how to answer that because even I don't know what's so interesting on my phone.

I have a bad case of anxiety that comes from not checking my phone. I spend most of my day on social media. I fear missing out on social media. I fear not being in the know of what everyone is discussing. I fear not being in the know of what my friends are posting on social media.

My mom thinks I'm addicted to my phone. Older people think teenagers like me have an addiction to their phones and computers. But I wouldn't say it's an addiction to a device. It's an addiction to social media. It's an addiction to being online, or in other words, a fear of not being online.

Basically, I have severe FOMO, for which I'm in desperate need of a cure. Maybe this spring break could be a chance to find one.

Part 2 My Two-week Detox
Day 1
So it was time to pull the plug. I grabbed my phone. I swiped it open and stared at the social media icons dotting the screen. I removed the apps from my phone. Then I moved to my notebook computer. I logged out of all of the social media sites. I felt an immediate sense of relief.

But soon after, I got restless. I don't remember how long it was, but I stared at my phone screen in complete confusion for quite a while. I called Jamie, and we chatted for about an hour. But there's only so much you can do over a voice call. We decided to meet later in the afternoon for a bike ride.

What else can I do on my phone? I lay on my bed even though I wasn't sleepy. I stayed there until I went out to meet Jamie. Throughout the day, it felt like things slowed down considerably. What a long day!

Day 4
I woke up late in the morning and reached for my phone. I swiped my phone open only to remember my social media apps were no longer there. Old habits die hard. After breakfast, I felt a strong urge to go online, to which I didn't want to give in. So, I decided to go out for a walk.

While walking in the park, I probably glanced at my phone 20 times. At one moment, I looked at the people around me, most of whom had their eyes glued to their phones. I moved my gaze upward and noticed how purely blue the sky was, without a single cloud in sight. All around the park, trees slowly swayed back and forth. Soon I found myself taking a couple of pictures of the peaceful scene.

After lunch, I took out my old guitar from under my bed. At first, it was because I was bored, but I ended up playing it all afternoon. It didn't matter that I'm not really good at it. It just felt great that I was lost in doing something for several hours without getting interrupted by my phone.

Day 7
I don't know why, but today I momentarily let down my guard against social media. As if bound by a spell, I logged into one of the social media sites, only to find that there was nothing interesting. I had a weird feeling of being at a place where I didn't belong, which was quickly replaced by a sense of guilt. I really shouldn't have gone back to a social media site in the middle of my detox.

Day 11
This was the first day my phone felt more like a brick in my pocket than a digital device. I could already feel free from worrying about posting something and hoping it would get some likes. At a gathering with my friends, it was fun to get asked over and over again about how I was surviving without social media. Sam said, "I don't think I could give up social media for even one day." My immediate thought was: Then you really need to give it up! I didn't actually say that, although I wanted to.

Day 14
Toward the end of the day, I reflected on my social media break and what things had been like before. I realized that social media had taken some control of me. It's kind of silly that all I did was envy others for their perfectly happy moments in life, dress up my everyday events, and think up ways to get others to like my posts. From now on, I want to be in control of how I use something or do something, not the other way around. Tomorrow, I will return to my social media activities, but in more careful and controlled ways. I'm going to stick to just a couple of sites that I really need, while making absolutely sure that my activities are in line with my well-being and happiness.

Read Further: Volunteering Online
Volunteering has a great deal of benefits. Not only do you make a positive impact on someone's life, but you gain valuable skills for your career. It even reduces stress and anxiety. With busy schedules, it can be hard to find the time to commit to volunteer work. These days, however, you can make a huge difference in the lives of others from your own home by virtually volunteering. Here are a few ways to virtually volunteer.

First, you could be a part of the effort to lend support to senior citizens who struggle with loneliness. Typically, volunteer "phone friends" make regular calls to chat and check in with these people. Second, you can help people with low or no vision with their everyday tasks. Through a live video call, you can offer visual assistance to those who need it with tasks such as reading "use by" dates and instructions on food packages, which helps them to lead more independent lives. Finally, if you have an interest in wildlife and its conservation, you can help with animal monitoring work by watching live videos of animal habitats around the world. Monitoring these animals helps protect wildlife and develop methods of conserving them.

Helping others and giving back to the community can be very rewarding. It can make your day more meaningful and productive. It is also a great way to connect with new people and cultures. For those who believe in karma, if you do good things for others, good things will happen to you!

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
"Yes," I look up from my phone to discover my mom [① yelling / ② yell] at me.

det.ref:
[원문] "Yes," I look up from my phone to discover my mom yelling at me.
[해석] "네," 나는 핸드폰에서 눈을 들어 엄마가 나에게 소리치고 있는 것을 알아차렸다. [문장 02 참고]
det.correct:
정답: ① yelling
지각동사(discover)는 「discover + O + V-ing(진행)」 또는 「discover + O + V원형」 구조를 취한다. 여기서 엄마가 "소리치고 있는 중"인 진행 상황을 강조하므로 현재분사 yelling이 적절하다.
wrongs: ① yelling ✅ — 지각동사 discover + O + V-ing: 진행 중인 동작 묘사
② yell ❌ — discover는 see/hear와 달리 V원형보다 V-ing가 자연스러움
det.tip:
💡 지각동사 + O + 보어
• see/hear/feel + O + V원형(동작 전체) / V-ing(진행)
• find/discover + O + V-ing(진행) 주로 사용

⚠️ 함정: discover는 원형보다 -ing가 훨씬 자연스러움

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
It's because my eyes are [① fixed / ② fixing] on my phone.

det.ref:
[원문] It's because my eyes are fixed on my phone.
[해석] 그것은 내 눈이 핸드폰에 고정되어 있기 때문이다. [문장 06 참고]
det.correct:
정답: ① fixed
「be fixed on」은 수동태로 "~에 고정되다"라는 의미. eyes는 fix의 대상(목적어 관계)이므로 과거분사 fixed가 적절하다.
wrongs: ① fixed ✅ — be + p.p.: 수동태. 눈이 고정"되는" 것
② fixing ❌ — be + V-ing(진행형)이면 "고정하고 있는 중"으로 의미 부적절
det.tip:
💡 be + p.p. vs. be + V-ing
• be fixed on: ~에 고정되다 (수동)
• be fixing: ~을 고정하는 중 (능동 진행)

⚠️ 주의: fix one's eyes on(능동) ↔ one's eyes are fixed on(수동)

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
I have a bad case of anxiety that comes from not [① checking / ② to check] my phone.

det.ref:
[원문] I have a bad case of anxiety that comes from not checking my phone.
[해석] 나는 핸드폰을 확인하지 않는 것에서 오는 심한 불안감이 있다. [문장 09 참고]
det.correct:
정답: ① checking
전치사 from 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 와야 한다. 「come from + V-ing」 = "~하는 것에서 비롯되다". 동명사의 부정은 not + V-ing.
wrongs: ① checking ✅ — 전치사 from + 동명사. not checking = 확인하지 않는 것
② to check ❌ — 전치사 뒤에 to부정사 불가
det.tip:
💡 전치사 + 동명사
• from/of/about/in + V-ing (전치사 뒤는 반드시 동명사)
• 동명사 부정: not + V-ing (not checking)

⚠️ 함정: to부정사와 혼동하기 쉬움. 전치사 뒤 = 항상 동명사!

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
Basically, I have severe FOMO, [① for which / ② which] I'm in desperate need of a cure.

det.ref:
[원문] Basically, I have severe FOMO, for which I'm in desperate need of a cure.
[해석] 기본적으로 나는 심각한 FOMO가 있고, 이에 대한 치료가 절실히 필요하다. [문장 17 참고]
det.correct:
정답: ① for which
원래 문장: I'm in desperate need of a cure for FOMO. 전치사 for가 관계대명사 앞으로 이동하여 「for which」가 된 것이다. be in need of a cure for ~: ~에 대한 치료가 필요하다.
wrongs: ① for which ✅ — 전치사+관계대명사: for FOMO → for which
② which ❌ — 전치사 for가 빠지면 문장 구조 불완전
det.tip:
💡 전치사 + 관계대명사
• 선행사 뒤 「전치사 + which/whom」 가능
• be in need of a cure for ~ → for which

⚠️ 시험 빈출: 전치사 + which vs. which 구별

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
I swiped it open and stared at the social media icons [① dotting / ② dotted] the screen.

det.ref:
[원문] I swiped it open and stared at the social media icons dotting the screen.
[해석] 나는 그것을 밀어 열고 화면에 점점이 흩어진 소셜 미디어 아이콘들을 응시했다. [문장 20 참고]
det.correct:
정답: ① dotting
icons와 dot은 능동 관계(아이콘들이 화면을 점점이 채우고 있음). 현재분사 dotting이 icons를 뒤에서 수식한다.
wrongs: ① dotting ✅ — 능동 관계: icons (are) dotting the screen → 현재분사
② dotted ❌ — 수동 관계가 아님. 아이콘이 화면을 점점이 "채우는" 것
det.tip:
💡 분사의 선택: 능동 vs. 수동
• 현재분사(-ing): 명사가 동작의 주체 (능동)
• 과거분사(-ed/p.p.): 명사가 동작의 대상 (수동)

⚠️ dot(점으로 채우다): icons dot the screen → icons dotting the screen

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
I [① lay / ② laid] on my bed even though I wasn't sleepy.

det.ref:
[원문] I lay on my bed even though I wasn't sleepy.
[해석] 졸리지 않았지만 침대에 누웠다. [문장 27 참고]
det.correct:
정답: ① lay
lie(눕다)의 과거형은 lay이다. laid는 lay(놓다)의 과거형. 문맥상 "침대에 누웠다"이므로 lie-lay-lain의 lay가 정답.
wrongs: ① lay ✅ — lie(눕다)의 과거형: lie-lay-lain
② laid ❌ — lay(놓다)의 과거형: lay-laid-laid. 타동사이므로 목적어 필요
det.tip:
💡 lie vs. lay 구별
• lie(눕다): lie-lay-lain-lying (자동사)
• lay(놓다): lay-laid-laid-laying (타동사)

⚠️ 최빈출 함정: lie의 과거형 lay ≠ lay의 현재형 lay

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
I swiped my phone open [① only to remember / ② only remembering] my social media apps were no longer there.

det.ref:
[원문] I swiped my phone open only to remember my social media apps were no longer there.
[해석] 핸드폰을 밀어 열었으나 소셜 미디어 앱이 더 이상 없다는 것만 기억해냈다. [문장 31 참고]
det.correct:
정답: ① only to remember
「only to V」는 "~했지만 결국 …하게 되다"라는 뜻의 결과 부사적 용법. 기대하지 않은 결과를 나타낸다.
wrongs: ① only to remember ✅ — 결과의 to부정사: 예상 밖의 결과 표현
② only remembering ❌ — only + V-ing는 결과의 부사적 용법으로 쓰이지 않음
det.tip:
💡 only to V (결과의 to부정사)
• 주로 부정적이거나 예상 밖의 결과
• He hurried to the station, only to find the train had left.

⚠️ 구별: only + to V(결과) vs. in order to V(목적)

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
I looked at the people around me, most of [① whom / ② who] had their eyes glued to their phones.

det.ref:
[원문] I looked at the people around me, most of whom had their eyes glued to their phones.
[해석] 나는 주변 사람들을 바라보았는데, 그들 대부분은 핸드폰에 눈을 붙이고 있었다. [문장 36 참고]
det.correct:
정답: ① whom
「전치사(of) + 관계대명사」 구조에서 전치사 뒤에는 whom(목적격)이 와야 한다. most of whom = 그들 중 대부분.
wrongs: ① whom ✅ — 전치사 of 뒤 목적격 관계대명사
② who ❌ — 전치사 뒤에 주격 who 불가
det.tip:
💡 전치사 + 관계대명사
• 전치사 + whom (사람) / which (사물)
• most of whom, some of which, all of whom

⚠️ 시험 함정: who vs. whom → 전치사 뒤는 반드시 whom

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
I noticed [① how purely blue the sky was / ② how the sky was purely blue], without a single cloud in sight.

det.ref:
[원문] I noticed how purely blue the sky was, without a single cloud in sight.
[해석] 나는 하늘이 얼마나 순수하게 파란지를 알아차렸다, 구름 한 점 없이. [문장 37 참고]
det.correct:
정답: ① how purely blue the sky was
감탄문이 간접 표현으로 쓰일 때 어순: 「how + 형용사/부사 + S + V」. purely blue가 형용사구로 how 바로 뒤에 위치한다.
wrongs: ① how purely blue the sky was ✅ — 간접의문문/감탄문: how + adj + S + V
② how the sky was purely blue ❌ — how 감탄문에서 형용사가 how 바로 뒤에 와야 함
det.tip:
💡 간접의문문/감탄문 어순
• how + 형용사/부사 + S + V
• I know how beautiful she is. (O)
• I know how she is beautiful. (X)

⚠️ what 감탄문: what + (a/an) + adj + 명사 + S + V

ch: ① how purely blue the sky was
② how the sky was purely blue

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
[① As if bound / ② As if binding] by a spell, I logged into one of the social media sites.

det.ref:
[원문] As if bound by a spell, I logged into one of the social media sites, only to find that there was nothing interesting.
[해석] 마치 마법에 걸린 듯, 나는 소셜 미디어 사이트 중 하나에 로그인했다. [문장 44 참고]
det.correct:
정답: ① As if bound
주어 I와 bind는 수동 관계(내가 마법에 묶이다). 분사구문에서 수동이면 「as if + p.p.」를 사용한다. bound는 bind의 과거분사.
wrongs: ① As if bound ✅ — 수동: I was bound by a spell → As if bound
② As if binding ❌ — 능동: "내가 마법을 묶는 중"이면 의미 부적절
det.tip:
💡 분사구문의 능동/수동
• 능동: As if knowing the answer, she smiled.
• 수동: As if surprised by the news, he froze.

⚠️ by + 행위자 → 수동(p.p.)의 강력한 단서

questions.stem:
다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 것을 모두 고르시오.
But soon after, I got restless. I don't remember how long it was, but I stared at my phone screen in complete confusion for quite a while. I called Jamie, and we chatted for about an hour. But there's only so much you can do over a voice call. We decided to meet later in the afternoon for a bike ride. What else can I do on my phone? I ⓐ lay on my bed even though I wasn't sleepy. I stayed there until I went out to meet Jamie. ⓑ Throughout the day, it felt like things ⓒ slowed down considerably. ⓓ How a long day!

det.ref:
[원문] What a long day! [문장 29 참고]
[해석] 정말 긴 하루였어!
det.correct:
정답: ⓓ How → What
감탄문 구조: 「What + (a/an) + 형용사 + 명사 + S + V!」. a long day는 "관사+형용사+명사"이므로 What이 맞다. How는 「How + 형용사/부사 + S + V!」 구조.
wrongs: ⓐ lay ✅ — lie(눕다)의 과거형 lay, 정상
ⓑ Throughout ✅ — "~내내" 전치사, 정상
ⓒ slowed ✅ — slow down의 과거형, 정상
ⓓ How ❌ → What: 감탄문에서 명사(a long day) 앞은 What
det.tip:
💡 What vs. How 감탄문
• What + (a/an) + adj + 명사: What a beautiful day!
• How + adj/adv: How beautiful the day is!

⚠️ 핵심: 명사 유무로 판단! 명사 있으면 What, 없으면 How

questions.stem:
다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
After breakfast, I felt a strong urge to go online, ⓐ to which I didn't want to give in. So, I decided ⓑ going out for a walk. While walking in the park, I probably ⓒ glanced at my phone 20 times.

det.ref:
[원문] So, I decided to go out for a walk. [문장 34 참고]
[해석] 그래서 나는 산책하러 나가기로 결심했다.
det.correct:
정답: ⓑ going → to go
decide는 to부정사를 목적어로 취하는 동사이다. 「decide to V」가 올바른 구조.
wrongs: ⓐ to which ✅ — give in to ~에서 전치사 to가 관계대명사 앞으로 이동, 정상
ⓑ going ❌ → to go: decide + to V (동명사 불가)
ⓒ glanced ✅ — glance at의 과거형, 정상
det.tip:
💡 to부정사만 목적어로 취하는 동사
• decide/hope/wish/want/plan/expect + to V
• 암기법: 미래지향적 동사 → to부정사

⚠️ 반대: enjoy/mind/finish/avoid + V-ing (동명사만)

questions.stem:
다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
Toward the end of the day, I reflected on my social media break and what things had been like before. I realized that social media ⓐ had taken some control of me. It's kind of silly that all I did was ⓑ envying others for their perfectly happy moments in life, ⓒ dress up my everyday events, and think up ways to get others to like my posts.

det.ref:
[원문] ...all I did was envy others for their perfectly happy moments in life, dress up my everyday events...
[해석] 내가 한 것이라곤 다른 사람들의 완벽하게 행복한 순간을 부러워하고, 일상을 꾸미고... [문장 54 참고]
det.correct:
정답: ⓑ envying → envy
「all S did was + V원형」 구문에서 was 뒤에는 동사원형이 온다. envy, dress, think up이 병렬구조로 모두 원형.
wrongs: ⓐ had taken ✅ — 과거완료: reflected(과거)보다 앞선 시점의 일, 정상
ⓑ envying ❌ → envy: all I did was + V원형

정답: envy

Selena suffered from FOMO and decided to do a two-week social media (A) d_______. Through this experience, she learned to be in control of her social media use.

det.tip:
💡 요약문 빈칸 전략

• 제목/소제목에서 중요 단어 파악

⚠️ detox = 해독, 독소 제거 → 소셜 미디어를 끊는 행위를 비유적으로 표현

questions.stem: 윗글을 읽고 추론할 수 없는 내용은?

det.ref:
[원문] I called Jamie, and we chatted for about an hour.
[해석] 나는 Jamie에게 전화했고, 약 한 시간 동안 수다를 떨었다. [문장 25 참고]
det.correct:
정답: ③ Selena의 친구 Jamie도 소셜 미디어 디톡스를 함께 시작했다.
Jamie에게 전화하고 자전거를 타러 만났다는 내용은 있지만, Jamie가 함께 디톡스를 했다는 언급은 전혀 없다.
wrongs: ① ✅ 추론 가능 — 엄마 말을 못 듣는 장면에서 추론 가능
② ✅ 추론 가능 — "took out my old guitar" = 예전 기타를 다시 꺼냄
③ ❌ 추론 불가 — Jamie의 디톡스 여부는 언급 없음
④ ✅ 추론 가능 — "a sense of guilt", "shouldn't have gone back"
⑤ ✅ 추론 가능 — "return to my social media activities, but in more careful ways"
det.tip:
💡 추론 불가 문제 전략
• 본문에 근거가 있는 선지 vs. 없는 선지 구별
• "언급 없음" ≠ "거짓"이 아니라 "추론 불가"

⚠️ 함정: 그럴듯해 보이지만 본문에 근거가 없는 선지 주의

questions.stem:
윗글의 주제를 다음과 같이 쓸 때 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 쓰시오.
How to overcome FOMO and take ( ___ ) of social media use through a digital detox

(1단어, 영문 7자, c로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] I want to be in control of how I use something or do something, not the other way around.
[해석] 나는 무언가를 사용하거나 하는 방식을 통제하고 싶다, 그 반대가 아니라. [문장 55 참고]
det.correct:
정답: control
글의 핵심 메시지는 소셜 미디어에 대한 통제력(control)을 되찾는 것. "be in control of"가 핵심 표현.
det.tip:
💡 주제 빈칸 전략
• 글의 결론 부분에서 핵심 키워드 찾기
• "in control of" = 핵심 메시지

⚠️ control vs. charge: be in control of(통제하다) / be in charge of(담당하다)
